note.explanation: Count every atom shown in the structural formula, write each element symbol, and use the atom counts as subscripts. Omit any subscript of 1.
examples: CH₃—C(=O)—O—H contains 2 C, 4 H and 2 O atoms, so its formula is C₂H₄O₂.
CH₃—CH₂—CH₂—OH contains 3 C, 8 H and 1 O atom, so its formula is C₃H₈O.
note.simple: A structural formula shows how atoms are joined. Count each kind of atom to write the molecular formula.
note.checkQuestion: What is the molecular formula of CH₃—CH₂—OH?
note.title: Getting a molecular formula from a structural formula
steps: Write down the structural formula of the compound.
Count the number of atoms of each type in the structural formula.
Write the symbols of all the elements.
Write the total number of atoms of each kind as a subscript.
note.answer: Write the symbol of each element and its atom count as a subscript; do not write a subscript 1.

mcqs.stem: What is the molecular formula of CH₃—CH₂—OH?
rationales: This is correct because the structure has 2 carbon, 6 hydrogen and 1 oxygen atom.
This is wrong because the structure has only 1 oxygen atom.
This is wrong because the structure has only 2 carbon atoms.
This is wrong because the structure has 6 hydrogen atoms, not 5.

mcqs.stem: A structural formula contains one carbon atom, four hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Which is its molecular formula?
rationales: This is correct because the subscripts show 1 C, 4 H and 1 O, with the subscript 1 omitted.
This is wrong because it has only 2 hydrogen atoms.
This is wrong because it has only 3 hydrogen atoms.
This is wrong because it has 2 carbon atoms and 4 hydrogen atoms.

mcqs.stem: A structural formula of phosphoric acid shows three OH groups, one P atom and one additional O atom double-bonded to P. What is its molecular formula?
rationales: This is correct because the structure has 3 H, 1 P and 4 O atoms.
This is wrong because it leaves out the hydrogen atoms in the three OH groups.
This is wrong because the structure contains 4 oxygen atoms, not 3.
This is wrong because the three OH groups contribute 3 hydrogen atoms, not 4.

mcqs.stem: Count the atoms in CH₃—CH₂—CH₂—OH. Which molecular formula is correct?
rationales: This is correct because the structure contains 3 C, 8 H and 1 O atom.
This is wrong because the hydrogen in the OH group must also be counted.
This is wrong because the structure contains 3 carbon atoms.
This is wrong because the structure contains only 1 oxygen atom.

mcqs.stem: A structural formula shows one calcium atom, one carbon atom and three oxygen atoms. What formula should be written?
rationales: This is correct because it shows 1 Ca, 1 C and 3 O atoms, omitting subscripts of 1.
This is wrong because it gives 3 carbon atoms and only 1 oxygen atom.
This is wrong because it gives only 2 oxygen atoms.
This is wrong because it gives 2 calcium atoms.

mcqs.stem: A structural formula contains 2 carbon, 4 hydrogen and 2 oxygen atoms. Which molecular formula follows?
rationales: This is correct because it records all three atom counts accurately.
This is wrong because it records only 1 oxygen atom.
This is wrong because it records only 3 hydrogen atoms.
This is wrong because it records only 1 carbon and 1 oxygen atom.

written.text: Write down the molecular formula of sulphuric acid. Its structural formula is: [H—O—S—O—H, with one O double-bonded above S and one O double-bonded below S.]

rubric.why: Correct atom counting is the basis of the formula.
rubric.how: State that the structure has 2 H, 1 S and 4 O atoms.

rubric.why: The final formula must show the correct counts and omit the subscript 1.

modelAnswer: It has 2 H, 1 S and 4 O atoms.
Its molecular formula will be H₂SO₄.

written.text: Write down the molecular formula of acetic acid. Its structure formula is: [CH₃—C(=O)—O—H.]

rubric.why: The formula depends on counting every atom in the structural formula.
rubric.how: State that it has 2 C, 4 H and 2 O atoms.

rubric.why: The final formula must represent all the atom counts correctly.

modelAnswer: Its molecular formula will be C₂H₄O₂

written.text: Find out the molecular formula of phosphoric acid, Its structural formula is: [P at the centre, with three OH groups and one double-bonded O.]

rubric.why: The structural formula must be counted before writing the formula.
rubric.description: Counts the atoms in the structure.
rubric.how: Identify 3 H, 1 P and 4 O atoms.

rubric.why: Correct subscripts give the molecular formula.
rubric.how: Write H₃PO₄, omitting the subscript 1 for P.

modelAnswer: It has 3 H, 1 P and 4 O atoms.
Its molecular formula will be H₃PO₄.

written.text: Determine the molecular formula of n – propyl alcohol. Its structural formula is CH₃—CH₂—CH₂—OH

rubric.why: Each atom, including the H in OH, must be counted.
rubric.description: Counts the atoms in the structural formula.
rubric.how: Identify 3 C, 8 H and 1 O atom.

rubric.why: Writing the atom counts as subscripts gives the required formula.
rubric.how: Write C₃H₈O and omit the subscript 1 for O.

modelAnswer: It has 3 C, 8 H and 1 O atom.
Its molecular formula will be C₃H₈O.

written.text: Write down the formula of calcium carbonate. Its structural formula is: [C at the centre, double-bonded to O and single-bonded to two O⁻ atoms; Ca²⁺ is also shown.]

rubric.why: The formula must reflect the number of each atom shown.
rubric.how: Identify 1 Ca, 1 C and 3 O atoms.

rubric.why: The correct formula uses subscripts for counts greater than 1 and omits subscript 1.

modelAnswer: It has 1 Ca, 1 C and 3 O atoms.

examTips: This section is commonly tested by asking you to count atoms from a structural formula and write the molecular formula.
Show the atom counts before writing the final formula; this makes your method clear and can earn a working mark.
Write the element symbols in the correct order and use subscripts for counts greater than 1.
Do not write a subscript 1 after an element symbol.

hints: Count the H atoms in each OH group.
There are three OH groups, one P atom and one additional double-bonded O atom.
yourTurn.question: Find out the molecular formula of phosphoric acid, Its structural formula is: [P at the centre, with three OH groups and one double-bonded O.]
solution: Write down the structural formula of phosphoric acid.
It has 3 H, 1 P and 4 O atoms.
Write the symbols of all the elements: H, P and O.
Write the total number of atoms of each kind as a subscript: H₃P₁O₄.

hints: Add the hydrogen atoms from all three carbon groups and the OH group.
yourTurn.question: Determine the molecular formula of n – propyl alcohol. Its structural formula is CH₃—CH₂—CH₂—OH
solution: Write down the structural formula of n-propyl alcohol: CH₃—CH₂—CH₂—OH.
It has 3 C, 8 H and 1 O atom.
Write the symbols of all the elements: C, H and O.
Write the total number of atoms of each kind as a subscript: C₃H₈O₁.

steps.text: It has 2 H, 1 S and 4 O atoms.

steps.why: Writing these counts as subscripts gives the molecular formula, with the subscript 1 omitted.
steps.text: Its molecular formula will be H₂SO₄

example.question: Write down the molecular formula of sulphuric acid. Its structural formula is: [H—O—S—O—H, with one O double-bonded above S and one O double-bonded below S.]

explain.title: Start with the structure
explain.body: A structural formula shows the atoms in a compound and how they are connected. Look at the whole structure before writing the formula.

explain.title: Count each kind of atom
explain.body: Count all atoms of one element, then all atoms of the next element. Include atoms in groups such as OH.

explain.title: Use subscripts
explain.body: Write each element symbol with its atom count as a subscript. If there is only one atom, omit the subscript 1.

mistakes: Forgetting to count an H atom in an OH group.
Missing an oxygen atom shown with a double bond.
Writing the number 1 as a subscript.
Using the number of groups instead of counting the atoms in every group.
